card.name: Moribayasa
card.era: Very old traditional rhythm and dance
card.tagline: Malinke solo women's liberation and thanksgiving dance
card.profile: Moribayasa is a very old rhythm and dance of the Malinke (Mandinka) of northeastern Guinea, performed by a woman who has overcome a major hardship such as infertility or serious illness, fulfilling a vow (Tontinkan; Wikipedia). Such a vow can be taken only once in a lifetime. For the dance the woman wears old, torn clothes and is allowed to break taboos; accompanied by djembe and dunun, she dances around the village from one tree (often a mango or the 'Moribayasa' tree) to another, then buries or leaves the rags behind the tree (Mama Lisa; Mamady Keita, A Life for the Djembe).
card.insight: Master drummer Famoudou Konate and others spread Moribayasa internationally through workshops and tours; Mamady Keita's book documents that the vow is so significant a woman may take it only once (Grokipedia; thesmith.org.uk).
card.image_significance: The dance of a woman who overcame. A representative image shows drum-driven communal movement, often in a circle with vivid textiles — Malinke, Guinea.
